text.title: Agent Invocation Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether the invocation leaves the repo for an external search provider, whether several stages share one quota, and how large the return payload is — to the full invocation config, a reduced local-only config, or skip when there is no agent loop to bound.

decision-tree.root-question: Does the invocation reach outside the repository — WebSearch, WebFetch or a search API — or does it stay on local files?

branch.when: a single deterministic tool call with a known target (read one file, hit one known endpoint) and no iteration

conclusion.verdict: skip; there is no loop to bound and no tool budget to constrain — make the call inline rather than wrapping it in a subagent config

branch.when: the subagent iterates but only over local files (Read, Grep, Glob) and returns a short answer to the parent
branch.question: Does the expected return exceed roughly a few thousand tokens, or does it fit in a short summary?

branch.when: the return is a short answer or a small structured object

conclusion.verdict: apply the reduced config: enumerate the read-only tool set explicitly instead of inheriting the parent's, set both an iteration cap and a stop condition, and validate the return caller-side

branch.when: the run produces a large transcript, file inventory or extracted corpus

conclusion.verdict: apply with a declared write path; the subagent returns that path plus a summary, and the single Write is scoped to it in `tools_whitelist`

branch.when: the subagent queries an external search or fetch provider
branch.question: Do two or more stages share one provider key or the built-in WebSearch quota, or is this one standalone invocation?

branch.when: one standalone invocation against the provider

conclusion.verdict: apply; the prompt forbids estimation, every external figure carries a URL the agent itself fetched, missing data is written as the literal 'Data not available', and the caller validates against `output_schema` before consuming

branch.when: several stages fan out over one shared key or quota

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology; stages run sequentially with each passing the previous stage's output path, every stage writes raw output to its declared path, and `trace_contract` records `stop_reason` and `iterations_used`
